plan: Fill the graveyard, sacrifice creatures for value, and bring the best of them back with Meren every end step.

maybeboard.name: Sheoldred, Whispering One
maybeboard.why: A second Meren on a body: it reanimates every upkeep and makes each opponent sacrifice a creature, which the review found the deck had no way to do. Woodfall Primus is the deck's only card at mana value 8 and its entry trigger is covered by Krosan Grip, Assassin's Trophy, Pernicious Deed and Acidic Slime.

maybeboard.name: Toxic Deluge
maybeboard.why: Mass disruption is at 5 against a target of 6. A scalable sweeper that kills through toughness, and Meren is the one player who profits from it: experience counters from her own creatures dying and a full graveyard for the end step. Splinterfright has no entry or death trigger worth rebuying.

swaps.why: Ramp was at 5 against a target of 10; Mesmeric Fiend gives the exiled card back when it is sacrificed, and Plan was at 40 against 30.
A recurring body beats a one-shot dig: Meren returns it every end step, and it is fodder for the sacrifice outlets, Victimize and Dread Return.
Lands was at 37 against a target of 38 and black at 58 pips against 24 sources; Mulch was the most redundant self-mill now that Satyr Wayfinder is in.
Lands was at 37 against a target of 38. Moldgraf Monstrosity costs mana value 7, returns two random creatures, and exiles itself so Meren can never rebuy it.

review.text:
**How it wins.** Turns 1 to 3 are still setup, and the curve is still bottom-heavy: 1 card at mana value 0, 6 at 1, 16 at 2 and 24 at 3, with an average mana value of 3.0. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet and Golgari Signet for the early mana; Stitcher's Supplier, Satyr Wayfinder, Stinkweed Imp, Golgari Grave-Troll and Life from the Loam to fill the graveyard; Carrion Feeder and Viscera Seer as free repeatable sacrifice outlets. Gravecrawler and Bloodghast are the bodies that do not mind dying.

Turns 4 to 6 are the deck. Meren of Clan Nel Toth costs 4; every other creature of yours that dies gives an experience counter, and each end step she returns a creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield if its mana value is no more than your experience counters, and otherwise puts it into your hand. The cards that cash that in are the entry and death triggers worth repeating — Fleshbag Marauder, Plaguecrafter, Ravenous Chupacabra, Shriekmaw, Acidic Slime, Reclamation Sage, and now Farhaven Elf and Satyr Wayfinder, which make Meren's end step a land or a self-mill every turn. Victimize, Dread Return, Animate Dead and Necromancy do the same work without her. Grave Pact, Dictate of Erebos and Butcher of Malakir turn each sacrifice into a table-wide edict.

Turns 7 and on: Living Death as the mass reset, Massacre Wurm as a sweeper that drains, Harvester of Souls at 6, and a top end that is now 1 card at mana value 7 and 1 at 8 rather than two sevens and an eight.

**What ends the game is still the weakest link.** Blood Artist and Zulaport Cutthroat are the cards that turn the dying into life loss, and 30 creatures with no evasion and no mass pump make for a slow attack. Nothing added in the improvements changed this: the deck strips a table of resources and then wins by attrition. Sheoldred, Whispering One sits on the maybeboard against Woodfall Primus precisely for this — an opponent sacrifice every upkeep is the closest thing to a clock the deck can reach from here.

**Curve against lands and ramp.** Lands is at 38 against a target of 38 — the Swamp that came in for Mulch closed that — and an average mana value of 3.0 fits it. Ramp is at 7 against a target of 10 after Farhaven Elf and Kodama's Reach: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Golgari Signet, Sakura-Tribe Elder, Cultivate, Farhaven Elf, Kodama's Reach. That is the one structural gap left, and it still matters, because a 4-mana commander who is killed repeatedly has to be recast on time. Targeted disruption is at 16 against a target of 12, and the stack of near-interchangeable two- and three-mana creature removal (Doom Blade, Murder, Go for the Throat, Infernal Grasp, Hero's Downfall) is where the last three ramp slots live. Your collection still holds Rampant Growth, Mind Stone, Fellwar Stone, Commander's Sphere, Burnished Hart, Wood Elves and Explosive Vegetation for them.

**Colours.** Black is at 56 pips against 25 sources, green at 25 pips against 21 sources. The extra Swamp helped, and black is still the deeper commitment — Grave Pact, Dictate of Erebos, Massacre Wurm and Butcher of Malakir all want more than one black. The nonbasic fixing is good: Command Tower, Overgrown Tomb, Woodland Cemetery, Twilight Mire, Llanowar Wastes, Golgari Rot Farm, Temple of Malady, Jungle Hollow, Golgari Guildgate.

**When Meren is answered.** The deck keeps running: Phyrexian Arena, Deathreap Ritual, Fecundity, Grim Haruspex, Midnight Reaper and Harvester of Souls draw without her, and Victimize, Dread Return, Animate Dead, Necromancy and Living Death recur without her. There is still no way to protect her and no way to find her — Demonic Tutor was the obvious answer and was left out because it is a Game Changer the bracket target of 2 does not allow.

**Categories.** Lands at 38 against a target of 38; Ramp at 7 against a target of 10; Card advantage at 11 against a target of 12; Targeted disruption at 16 against a target of 12; Mass disruption at 5 against a target of 6; Plan at 38 against a target of 30. Plan came down from 40 and the deck is better for it: the cards that left (Mesmeric Fiend, Grisly Salvage, Moldgraf Monstrosity, Mulch) were the ones serving the plan most thinly. Theme density is 38 of 99.

Two cards are still counted on a stretch. Viscera Seer counts in Card advantage, but scry 1 on a sacrifice filters the top of your library rather than turning one card into more than one — it is a sacrifice outlet first, and Card advantage at 11 against 12 is really at 10 in spirit. Spore Frog counts in Mass disruption, where preventing all combat damage answers a whole attack, but once; its real job is to be recurred by Meren as a fog every turn, which is Plan work. Mass disruption at 5 against 6 is therefore the softest count in the deck, and Toxic Deluge is on the maybeboard against Splinterfright to fix it.

**The land that makes no mana.** Evolving Wilds, which taps and sacrifices itself to fetch a basic land onto the battlefield tapped — with basics of both types in the deck it always has a target, and the land entering triggers Bloodghast.

**Bracket.** The target is 2 and the deck sits at 2, with no Game Changers.
